kicker: Ember · Science · Test on Wed 18 Nov
title: Days 1–2: Pressure
sub: Day 1 (Wed): pressure on solids, P = F ÷ A. Day 2 (Thu): pressure in gases and the atmosphere. About 25 minutes each day.
skill: The Because Chain: cause → effect → consequence.
target: Every pressure explanation needs the link: smaller area → the same force is more concentrated → bigger pressure. For gases: more collisions with the walls → bigger pressure.

sections.sub: Pressure is how concentrated a force is: how much force pushes on each bit of area.

blocks.html:
The equation
pressure = force ÷ area

Units: force in newtons (N). Area in m² gives pressure in N/m², which is also called the pascal (Pa): 1 N/m² = 1 Pa. Area in cm² gives pressure in N/cm².

Same force, smaller area → bigger pressure. Same force, bigger area → smaller pressure.

blocks.q: You push a drawing pin into a board with the same force each time. Where is the pressure on the board biggest?
o: Under the flat head, if you push it in upside down
The same: the force is the same
blocks.why: The point has a tiny area, so the same force is concentrated on a small area: the pressure is huge and it goes into the board.

blocks.q: Which unit is the same as 1 N/m²?
blocks.why: 1 pascal is 1 newton on each square metre. N/cm² is a different, much bigger unit (1 N/cm² = 10 000 N/m²).

blocks.q: Why do snowshoes stop you sinking into deep snow?
o: They spread your weight over a bigger area, so the pressure on the snow is smaller
They increase the force on the snow
blocks.why: Your weight (the force) is the same. Spreading it over a bigger area makes the pressure smaller, so the snow is not pushed down as much.

sections.sub: Write the equation, put the numbers in, then the answer with its unit.

blocks.q: A box with a weight of 300 N rests on the floor. Its base has an area of 0.5 m². Calculate the pressure on the floor.

traps.msg: Upside down: force goes on top, area underneath.

blocks.q: A skater with a weight of 600 N stands on one skate blade. The blade touches the ice over an area of 0.0005 m². Calculate the pressure.
blocks.why: pressure = 600 ÷ 0.0005 = 1 200 000 N/m². A tiny area makes a huge pressure, which is why the blade cuts into the ice.

traps.msg: You multiplied. Divide the force by the area.

blocks.q: A brick with a weight of 24 N rests on a shelf. The face touching the shelf has an area of 120 cm². Calculate the pressure in N/cm².
blocks.why: pressure = 24 ÷ 120 = 0.2 N/cm². With area in cm² the unit is N/cm².

traps.msg: Upside down: it is force ÷ area, 24 ÷ 120.

blocks.html: Finding the force. If you know the pressure and the area: force = pressure × area. (This is pressure = force ÷ area, rearranged: multiply both sides by the area.)

blocks.q: An elephant’s feet press on the ground with a pressure of 100 000 N/m². The total area of its feet is 0.4 m². Calculate the force (its weight).

traps.msg: You divided. To find the force, multiply pressure by area.

blocks.q: A suction cup has an area of 0.02 m². The air presses on it with a pressure of 100 000 N/m². What force holds it on?
A force of 50 N makes a pressure of 2500 N/m². What area is it acting on, in m²?

sections.sub: A Because Chain: one mark per link.

blocks.q: Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt one? Tap the links in order.
items: A sharp knife has a very thin edge, so its area is small.
So the same force acts on a smaller area.
So the pressure on the food is bigger.
So the knife pushes through the food more easily.
blocks.done: Cause (small area) → effect (bigger pressure) → consequence (cuts easily).

blocks.q: A tractor has very wide tyres. Explain why this helps it drive over soft, muddy fields without sinking.

points.t: wide tyres have a bigger area touching the ground
so the tractor’s weight is spread out / the same force acts on a bigger area
so the pressure on the ground is smaller, so it sinks less

starters: The wide tyres have a bigger…

sections.sub: Read this, then answer from memory.

blocks.html:
Why a gas presses. A gas (or a liquid) is a fluid: it has no fixed shape. Its particles move about quickly and collide with the walls of the container. Each collision pushes on the wall. All those pushes make the gas pressure. The particles move in every direction, so the pressure acts in all directions: that is why a balloon swells in every direction.

Squash it (smaller volume): the particles hit the walls more often → higher pressure.
Heat it: the particles move faster, so they hit the walls harder and more often → higher pressure.

Atmospheric pressure is the pressure of the air all around us. We do not feel it because the fluids inside our body push out just as hard. Higher up a mountain there is less air above you, so its weight is less and the air is less dense: atmospheric pressure is lower, and each breath holds less oxygen.

blocks.q: In which direction does the pressure of a gas act?
blocks.why: The particles move and collide in every direction, so the pressure acts in all directions.

blocks.q: You push in the handle of a bike pump with your finger over the end. What happens to the air pressure inside, and why?
o: It goes down, because there is less air
It goes up, because the particles are closer together and hit the walls more often
It stays the same, because there is the same amount of air
blocks.why: Same number of particles in a smaller volume → more collisions with the walls each second → higher pressure.

blocks.q: A sealed can of air is heated. Why does the pressure inside rise?
o: The particles move faster, so they hit the walls harder and more often
blocks.why: Heating gives the particles more energy: faster particles collide harder and more often. The particles themselves do not get bigger.

blocks.q: Why is atmospheric pressure lower at the top of a mountain?
o: There is less air above you pressing down, and the air is less dense
blocks.why: Less air above you means less weight of air pushing down. Gravity pulls air towards the Earth, so it is densest at sea level.

blocks.q: The gas in a balloon pushes with a force of 6 N on an area of 0.0002 m². Calculate the gas pressure.
blocks.why: pressure = 6 ÷ 0.0002 = 30 000 N/m². Fluid pressure uses the same equation.

traps.msg: You multiplied. Divide force by area.

blocks.q: Why does a balloon get bigger when you blow more air into it? Tap the links in order.
items: There are more air particles inside the balloon.
So there are more collisions on the inside of the rubber than on the outside.
So the pressure inside is bigger than the pressure outside.
So the rubber is pushed outwards in all directions.
blocks.done: More particles → more collisions → higher pressure inside → the balloon stretches.

blocks.q: A sealed bag of crisps is taken up a mountain. The bag puffs up. Explain why.

points.t: higher up, atmospheric pressure is lower (less air above / air less dense)
the air inside the bag now has a higher pressure than the air outside
so the gas pushes the bag outwards (in all directions)

starters: so the air inside the bag…

blocks.q: Explain why a car tyre’s pressure goes up after a long drive, when the tyre is hot.

points.t: the air inside gets hotter, so its particles move faster
they hit the walls of the tyre harder and more often

starters: The air in the tyre gets hotter, so…

items: I can write pressure = force ÷ area from memory, with units (N, m², N/m² = Pa).
I can find a force: force = pressure × area.
For gases I mention collisions with the walls.
I can say why air pressure is lower up a mountain.

blocks.q: “Why does a drawing pin go into the board but your thumb doesn’t hurt?”
blocks.note: For the parent: listen for the point has a small area so a big pressure; the head has a big area so a small pressure on the thumb, with the same force. If she just says “it’s sharp”, ask “what does sharp mean for the area?”
